objective: Every subcommand of the `stockroom` command line is spread over three places in `stockroom/cli.py`: its options are declared in `_parser`, its behaviour is a `_cmd_*` function, and a dict `COMMANDS` at the bottom maps its name to that function. Adding a command means editing all three and the help texts live apart from the code. Restructure `cli.py` so that each command is one record in a registry and both the argument parser and the dispatch are derived from that registry when `main` runs. This is a pure refactor for the four existing commands: their help texts, usage errors, results, error messages and exit codes stay byte for byte the same, and the existing tests keep passing without being edited.
acceptance: `stockroom.cli.Command` is a frozen dataclass with the fields `name`, `help`, `configure` and `run`, in this order (so `Command(name, help, configure, run)` works positionally and by keyword); `configure(parser)` declares the options of the command on its argparse subparser, and `run(args, config)` returns the exit code

`stockroom.cli.COMMANDS` is a `dict` from command name to `Command` holding `items`, `stock`, `sales` and `price`, in this order, with the help texts `list the catalogue`, `list items below their reorder level`, `sales summary` and `price a quantity of one item`

The parser and the dispatch are built from `COMMANDS` every time `main` runs: a `Command` added to the dict is parsed with its own `configure`, listed in `--help` with its `help` text, run with the loaded settings dict (defaults, then the `--config` file, then `STOCKROOM_*` variables) and, when it raises a `StockroomError`, ends with `stockroom: error: <message>` on stderr and exit code 1 after what it already printed; a command removed from the dict is rejected as an invalid choice with exit code 2; a replaced entry is parsed and run with the replacement's `configure` and `run`

For `items`, `stock`, `sales` and `price`, run through `cli.main` with the terminal width fixed at 80, the output of `--help` (main and every subcommand), `--version`, every usage error (missing options, a bad value, an unknown command, no command), the normal results, the data errors (exit code 1, message on stderr) and the handling of settings from the environment and from `--config` are identical to what they were before the change
